taskDescription: Arrange the steps of rabies pathogenesis in the correct sequence from virus entry to clinical disease.
paragraphs: Rabies virus enters through a bite wound and replicates locally at the inoculation site in muscle cells.
The virus binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction and enters peripheral nerve axons for retrograde axoplasmic transport toward the CNS.
The virus reaches the central nervous system and causes encephalitis, producing Negri bodies (eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions) in hippocampal and Purkinje neurons.
From the CNS, the virus descends centrifugally along peripheral nerves to reach the salivary glands, enabling transmission through saliva.
Clinical manifestations develop: hydrophobia, aerophobia, autonomic dysfunction and progressive paralysis leading to death.
